title: Automation Workflows knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Automation Workflows”?
options: Separating side effects from decision logic
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Turning manual procedures into scripts” under lesson 170, “Automation Workflows”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Automation Workflows”?
options: Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Preview high-impact changes, verify results, and document recovery.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
questions.answer_key: Preview high-impact changes, verify results, and document recovery.
questions.explanation: Preview high-impact changes, verify results, and document recovery. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Automation Workflows”?
options: Validate the exact target, use a preview for side effects, and verify the result before reporting success.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
questions.answer_key: Validate the exact target, use a preview for side effects, and verify the result before reporting success.
questions.explanation: Validate the exact target, use a preview for side effects, and verify the result before reporting success. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
